nv_oasis_the.blurb: A small sport crag in the Calico Hills of Red Rock, split into a left wall, a right wall and a short upper tier. Most of the thirteen routes are bolted, with a couple of trad lines mixed in, and the bulk of them sit in the 5.11 to 5.12 range with only a handful of easier pitches. The left wall and upper tier catch sun until late in the afternoon, while the right wall stays shaded until about midday, so you can pick a side for the weather. The corridor is fairly sheltered from wind. Reaching it takes some effort: expect a scrambly gully and a bit of fourth-class climbing, so it tends to be quiet.

nv_jabba_the_hutt_rock.blurb: A low sandstone crag in Calico Basin at Red Rock, sitting on the lower tier beneath a bigger east-facing cliff. Thirteen routes mix trad and sport with a single top-rope option, and most fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a couple of easy lines at the bottom and one 5.11 at the top. The walk in is short, ten minutes at most, which makes it a fitting after-work stop. The wall goes into shade from around noon, and it rarely gets crowded. Rock quality swings from route to route, so test holds before trusting them.

nv_blood_wall.blurb: A big dark red sandstone wall hanging below the western ridge of Cactus Flower Tower, high above Oak Creek Canyon at Red Rock. Nearly all of the thirteen routes are trad, several of them multi-pitch, with one aid line and one boulder problem. Difficulty runs from about 5.7 up through 5.12, with the middle of the range around 5.9 to 5.12. It sits on the north side of the ridge, so warm weather suits it best. The hike in is long and involves slabs and some brush, which keeps traffic low, but the better lines have excellent rock.

nv_disappearing_buttress.blurb: A roughly 500-foot sandstone buttress tucked into a small canyon just north of Illusion Crags in the southern outcrops of Red Rock. All thirteen routes are trad, from single pitches to multi-pitch lines, with grades from 5.6 to the low 5.11s and most sitting between 5.8 and 5.10. The south-facing cliff collects sun for much of the day even in midwinter. Road noise from the nearby highway carries in, yet the place feels private and little travelled. Descent is straightforward by way of a ledge system and a gully. Bring gear for building your own anchors.

nv_walden_cove.blurb: A sport wall on the Cathedral Rock south side in Kyle Canyon, up on Mount Charleston at around 7,900 feet, so it is a cooler alternative to the desert crags. It lies just east of the neighbouring Walden West section. Thirteen bolted routes, nearly all of them around 5.10 with a few 5.11s and a single 5.9, make it a good fit for climbers working through the 5.10 grades. A 40 m rope covers everything, and many routes begin with a high first bolt, so watch the opening moves. The routes carry space-themed names.
